newsitem.title: USA: Asset backeds and Spiders from Mars - Bowie's bonds.
newsitem.headline: Asset backeds and Spiders from Mars - Bowie's bonds.

text.p: David Bowie's not royalty, but his royalties still get special treatment.

The British Rock-and-Roller, with the help of U.S. brokerage firm Fahnestock & Co Inc, closed the first-ever music royalties future receivables securitization in the U.S. asset-backed market, said David Pullman, managing director of Fahnestock's structured finance group.
The deal featured $55 million in securities from DJT Royalty Financing Company, backed by a catalogue of Bowie songs, compositions and copyrights.
Retail investors were said to make a powerful try for the securities, but they were barred from the private placement.

Bowie's asset-backeds were deemed worthy of a single-A investment grade rating by one of the four major international rating agencies. The agency's name was withheld by Pullman because he prohibited it from making the rating public before the deal's completion.
Pullman, who created the asset class along with Bowie business manager Bill Zysblat of Rascof Zysblat Organisation, said he has more such deals lined up for the future.
The deal was originated by Gruntal & Co's Structured Asset Sales group headed by Pullman. The entire division was formally transferred over to Fahnestock in January.
